newsitem.title: FRANCE: French spending poor for fourth quarter outlook.
newsitem.headline: French spending poor for fourth quarter outlook.

text.p: Consumer spending on manufactured goods in France fell 2.6 percent in October after an expected plunge in car buying, but economists said this was not solely to blame and the data augured badly for fourth quarter consumption.

The October fall followed a revised fall of 1.6 percent in September. Spending on cars dropped 25.8 percent after the expiry of government incentives for car buyers, data from statistics institute INSEE showed.

The data coincided with an article in daily Liberation which quoted Bank of France monetary policy council member Paul Marchelli, one of a minority camp in the Bank believed to favour an easier monetary policy, as saying interest rates should be lowered as quickly as possible to boost growth.
Economists said that beyond the plunge in car buying, the data for retail spending showed a rise of only 3.1 percent, after a fall of 5.6 percent in September.

"The underlying number, retail, failed to show much of a bounce back. At best the underlying trend in consumption in France is flat. It's another indicator showing the concerns about the economy are not going away," said Sean Shepley, London-based economist at CS First Boston.
"It's a very big drop. The drop in car sales we knew about and it's not surprising," said David Naude, economist at JP Morgan investment bank in Paris.
"The trend remains weak, this is first data on the fourth quarter and confirms the quarter will be weak as a whole."
"We've still got a sluggish economy," said Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France.

"Once you take away any price advantage people can get things fall away. There's no support behind this trend although the whole picture will be blurred by (third quarter) GDP numbers this week which should be strong.

The government is counting on a revival in consumer spending and company investment to boost growth to 2.3 percent next year from 1.3 percent this year and help it reduce the budget deficit in preparation for European monetary union.
